text: Hormones treat reproductive disorders mainly in cattle and swine. To induce estrus: Estradiol (Corpuline) is used in gilts or heifers showing no heat signs (red vulva, interest from males) past normal puberty age; Prostaglandin (Lutalyse) can be injected in a cow not cycling after weaning her calf, since the ovary can be 'blocked' by a cyst — though very thin cattle need better feeding to recover condition rather than hormones. To induce delivery: if a sow hasn't farrowed by 115 days of gestation, Prostaglandin triggers farrowing a few hours later (the farmer must be sure of the mating date to calculate this correctly). To strengthen uterine contractions during delivery: piglets are normally born about every 20 minutes — if more than 30 minutes pass, injecting 1 ml Oxytocin into the muscle increases contraction strength and helps expel the next piglet. To help expel the placenta: injecting 2 ml Oxytocin into the muscle once farrowing is finished helps ensure the whole placenta is expelled in sows. To trigger milk ejection: Oxytocin stimulates milk let-down — in MMA (no milk) cases right after farrowing, injecting 0.5 ml Oxytocin is crucial to start milk and colostrum flow. To drain an infected uterus: Oxytocin only works during delivery itself — for uterine infection with discharge outside of delivery, Prostaglandin is used instead to trigger the contractions needed to expel infected material.
